blocks.p: An item card sets out what one item is and what can be done with it. To open the card for an item, click the item in an inventory list. The card opens in the drawer at the left of the window, on top of the panel that was there, and stays open until you click its close box or the action you started from it is done.
Cards are not only for items. A card also opens for a generator, a campfire, a farm plot, a trough, a padlock or a liquid.

Kind and weight. For food: hunger, thirst, cooked and freshness. For a weapon: condition, damage and reach.

Weapons only: damage, range, swing, knockback and critical chance.

blocks.note: Freshness and condition each end in a small square status mark.

blocks.p: Figure 21-1 shows two cards: the card for a piece of food and the card for a weapon. A card is read from the top down: the controls first, then the marks, then the facts, and last the facts that belong to that kind of item. Each fact is given on a line of its own, its name at the left and its value at the right. Food adds its nutrition facts and a weapon its combat facts; the rows are listed in Table 21-1.

blocks.p: To use an item from its card, click the main action in the top row. *More* lists the item's other actions. To close the card, click its close box; the panel it covered returns.

marks.text: The X closes the card. Top row: the main action (Eat, Equip) and More.
Marks: favorite, no-craft, dispose. Click a button to set one.
Condition, with a square status mark.
Combat facts: damage, range, swing, knockback, critical chance.

sticky.text: Click an item to open its card. Food gets a nutrition label!
